<details>
<summary>Changelog</summary>

- new advanced `-p, --pipe auto|always|never` (only in `-fh`): overrides
  the config's `pipe` for one run
- new configs have `theme = 'system'` in the `[gui]` section
- `deew-gui`/`deew-web` 1.0.0:
  - 1.0.0 because the GUI is considered complete and stable now
  - the theme button opens a menu with Light, Dark and System (follows
    the operating system); `deew-gui` saves the choice as `theme` in the
    `[gui]` section of the config (`'system'`, `'light'` or `'dark'`,
    default `'system'`), `deew-web` starts on System and each browser
    keeps its own choice

</details>

Dolby Encoding Engine Wrapper

English readme • Magyar leírás

## DDP encoding has never been so easy! ![img](website/terminal.gif) # Description - drives the command line tools of Dolby Encoding Engine 6.7 and creates the intermediate files in the background, giving you a proper tool - encodes DD, DDP, DDP Atmos, TrueHD, TrueHD Atmos, AC4, AC4 Atmos, AC4 IMS (immersive stereo) and AAC (always 2.0, mono inputs are rejected) - re-encodes TrueHD Atmos to DDP Atmos / TrueHD Atmos / AC4 Atmos from the Atmos master (raw `.thd` or a container like mkv/mka/m2ts, use `-ti` to select the track; decoded with truehdd, DDP Atmos and TrueHD Atmos use dee_shim to stop DEE smoothing the object positions a second time) - reads Dolby Atmos masters directly: ADM BWF (`.wav`/`.bwf` with `chna` and `axml` chunks) and DAMF (`.atmos` with its `.atmos.audio` and `.atmos.metadata`) go straight into DEE for `ddp-atmos`, `thd-atmos`, `ac4-atmos` and `ac4-ims` (no truehdd, no ffmpeg), and `-mo` measures them; `dd`/`ddp` get a 5.1 (or `-dm 2`/`1`) render of the master from DEE - runs multiple encodes in parallel for batch encoding (see config) - works on Windows, Linux and macOS - automatic sample rate conversion using ffmpeg's soxr resampler in case of an unsupported sample rate - for DD/DDP/AC4 unsupported rates will be converted to 48 kHz - for TrueHD unsupported rates will be converted to 48 kHz if source sample rate is lower than 72 kHz, otherwise will be converted to 96 kHz - automatic channel swapping for 7.1 sources (DEE swaps Ls Rs with Lrs Rrs for some reason) - automatically compensates for the delay of the encoders: 256 samples for DD/DDP, 2048 for AC4, 1710 / 1702 / 1600 for AAC (up to 71 / 72–87 / from 88 kbps), 32 more when DEE does the downmix (TrueHD has none) - works even with video inputs - AC4 `-dn` (loudness measurement) doesn't support 7.1 sources - versatile delay option that supports ms, s and also frame@fps formats, parsing delay from filenames also supported The [deew tool chain](https://deew.app/tool-chain) page shows how deew connects ffprobe, ffmpeg, truehdd, dee_shim and the DEE tools, with the exact options it passes to each one for every format. # Requirements - ffmpeg - ffprobe - [Dolby Encoding Engine 6.7](https://customer.dolby.com/content-creation-and-delivery/dolby-encoding-engine-v670) - [truehdd](https://github.com/truehdd/truehdd) (only for TrueHD Atmos sources of the Atmos formats: `ddp-atmos`, `thd-atmos`, `ac4-atmos`, `ac4-ims`; Atmos masters don't need it) - [dee_shim](https://github.com/truehdd/dee-shim) (only for `ddp-atmos`, `thd-atmos`, TrueHD with DRC `none` or at 96 kHz, the standard profile of 7.1 DDP and 7.0 DDP) - `ddp-atmos` and `thd-atmos` use it so DEE doesn't smooth the object positions of the TrueHD decode a second time, TrueHD with DRC `none` (the default) uses it because the TrueHD encoder has no `none` DRC preset; 96 kHz TrueHD (any DRC) is encoded through it with `--apodise off` so it stays lossless (DEE's own encoder applies its apodising filter to 96 kHz input, which changes every sample, so dee_shim is required for it) # Where deew looks for the programs deew looks for the programs in this order, there is nothing to set in the config: 1. next to the deew executable (the DEE tools in the `dee` folder next to it) 2. your PATH `deew -v` shows what it found and where. `deew -gt` / `deew --get-tools` downloads everything except DEE next to deew: ffmpeg, ffprobe, truehdd and dee_shim (ffmpeg is the latest stable GPL build from [BtbN](https://github.com/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds) on Windows/Linux and from [martin-riedl.de](https://ffmpeg.martin-riedl.de/) on macOS). DEE can't be downloaded, install it by hand (see below). ``` deew(.exe) ffmpeg(.exe), ffprobe(.exe), truehdd(.exe), dee_shim(.exe) dee/ (dee_ddp_encoder, dee_dthd_encoder, ... license.lic) ``` # Dolby Encoding Engine installation - install [VisualCppRedist AIO](https://github.com/abbodi1406/vcredist/releases) on Windows - install [DEE 6.7](https://customer.dolby.com/content-creation-and-delivery/dolby-encoding-engine-v670), use the version that matches your OS (Windows, Linux or macOS) - DEE 5.2.1 and older versions are not supported anymore - put the folder of the DEE tools (`dee_ddp_encoder`, `dee_ac4_encoder`, ...) next to deew and name it `dee`, or put the tools in your PATH - the Linux version of DEE doesn't include a TrueHD encoder (`dee_dthd_encoder`): [dthd-mac2linux](https://github.com/truehdd/dthd-mac2linux) can build a Linux `dee_dthd_encoder` from the macOS one, put it into the DEE folder - on Apple silicon the macOS tools need Rosetta 2 # deew (CLI) installation ### with standalone build (Windows 10-11/Linux/macOS): - grab the latest build (`deew` / `deew.exe` / `deew-macos`) from: [https://github.com/pcrlnd/deew/releases](https://github.com/pcrlnd/deew/releases) - on Linux/macOS make it executable: `chmod +x deew` (`chmod +x deew-macos` on macOS) - run with: `deew` (`deew.exe` on Windows, `deew-macos` on macOS)\ *(run the binary from terminal, doubleclicking it won't work)* - on the first run it will create a config file (the tools go next to deew or in your PATH, see above) - run `deew -gt` to download everything except DEE (ffmpeg, ffprobe, truehdd, dee_shim) next to deew - updating: grab the latest build from: [https://github.com/pcrlnd/deew/releases](https://github.com/pcrlnd/deew/releases) ### build from source (Windows/Linux/macOS): - install Rust if you don't have it already: [https://rustup.rs](https://rustup.rs) - run: `cargo install deew` - run with: `deew` - on the first run it will create a config file - updating: run the same command again: `cargo install deew` - after updating from deew 3.x or older generate a new config with `deew -gc` (the config format changed in 5.0.0) ### Usage - `deew -fh` (`deew -h` shows the same without the advanced `-sps`, `-lpf`, `-s3a`, `-wm` and `-bc`) ``` USAGE: deew [-h] [-fh] [-v] [-i [INPUT ...]] [-ti INDEX] [-o DIRECTORY] [-oi] [-on NAME] [-ot TEMPLATE] [-f FORMAT] [--ddp-mode MODE] [--ddp-atmos-mode MODE] [--ac4-ims-mode MODE] [-b BITRATE] [-dm CHANNELS] [-dl] [-sps SWITCH] [-lpf SWITCH] [-s3a SWITCH] [-wm MODE] [-bc SWITCH] [-d DELAY] [-r DRC] [-dn DIALNORM] [-in NUMBER] [-p MODE] [-k] [-kl] [-mo] [-lb] [-la] [-np] [-pl] [-cl] [-c] [-gc] [-gt] FLAGS: -h, --help show this help message. -fh, --full-help show all options, including the advanced ones -v, --version show version and the versions of the tools. -i, --input [INPUT ...] audio file(s) or folder(s) wildcards (*, ?, **) work, quoted or not ADM BWF and DAMF (.atmos) Atmos masters work for dd/ddp and the Atmos formats -ti, --track-index INDEX examples: 1, a:1, s:3 default: 0 select the audio track of input(s) N or a:N: Nth audio track, s:N: stream index N -o, --output DIRECTORY default: output path of the config, else the current directory specifies output directory -oi, --output-to-input save each output next to its input file overrides -o and the output path of the config -on, --output-name NAME name of the output file, one input file only -ot, --output-template TEMPLATE default: {stem}, config: output.template name of each output file, placeholders: {stem} (name without extension and delay tag) {name}, {format}, {codec}, {channels}, {bitrate} {lang}, {title} (of the audio track), {track} empty values drop out with a separator -f, --format FORMAT options: dd / ddp / ddp-atmos / thd / thd-atmos / ac4 / ac4-atmos / ac4-ims / aac default: ddp ddp-atmos and thd-atmos use truehdd and dee_shim, ac4-atmos and ac4-ims (from Atmos) use truehdd --ddp-mode MODE options: standard / bluray default: run -c/--config profile of 7.1 DDP, 5.1 and below are not affected standard: E-AC-3 only, 384-1792 kbps bluray: AC-3 core + E-AC-3, 768-1664 kbps --ddp-atmos-mode MODE options: streaming / standard / bluray default: run -c/--config profile of ddp-atmos streaming: 5.1 with Atmos, 384-1024 kbps standard: 7.1 with Atmos, E-AC-3 only, 768-2048 kbps bluray: 7.1 with Atmos, AC-3 core + E-AC-3, 1152-1664 kbps --ac4-ims-mode MODE options: general / music default: run -c/--config profile of ac4-ims (stereo for headphones and TV speakers, from 5.1 or Atmos) music: no dialogue enhancement, DRC music_light -b, --bitrate BITRATE options: run -lb/--list-bitrates default: run -c/--config -dm, --downmix CHANNELS options: 1 / 2 / 6 specifies downmix, only works for DD/DDP/AC4/AAC and TrueHD (2 / 6) DD, AC4 and ac4-ims will be automatically downmixed to 5.1 in case of a 7.1 source AAC output is always 2.0 -dl, --disable-lfe remove the LFE channel of 5.1 and 7.1 inputs DD and DDP get a real 5.0 or 7.0, the others keep a silent LFE 5.0 and 7.0 inputs are supported, they have no LFE -sps, --surround-phase-shift SWITCH options: on / off default: on DEE's 90° phase shift of the surround channels only works for DD/DDP/DDP Atmos, config: surround_phase_shift -lpf, --low-pass-filter SWITCH options: on / off default: on DEE's 120 Hz low-pass filter on the LFE channel only works for DD/DDP, config: low_pass_filter -s3a, --surround-3db-attenuation SWITCH options: on / off default: off 3 dB attenuation of the surround channels only works for DD/DDP/TrueHD, config: surround_3db_attenuation TrueHD asks first: the output is no longer identical to the source -wm, --warp-mode MODE options: normal / warping / prologiciix / loro default: from the source's metadata truehdd's warp mode, only used when the TrueHD Atmos source has none config: truehdd_warp_mode -bc, --bed-conform SWITCH options: on / off default: off truehdd's bed conformance, for Atmos sources whose bed comes out as objects config: truehdd_bed_conform -d, --delay DELAY examples: -5.1ms, +1,52s, -24@pal, +10@24000/1001 default: 0ms or parsed from filename specifies delay as ms, s or frame@FPS FPS can be a number, division or ntsc / pal you have to specify negative values as -d=-0ms -r, --drc DRC options: none / film_light / film_standard / music_light / music_standard / speech default: none (music_light for AC4) specifies drc profile none uses dee_shim for TrueHD, not available for AC4 (AC4 Atmos and ac4-ims have it) -dn, --dialnorm DIALNORM options: between -31 and 0 (in case of 0 DEE's measurement will be used) default: 0 applied dialnorm value, doesn't work for AAC, AC4 Atmos and ac4-ims -in, --instances NUMBER examples: 1, 4, 50% default: 50% specifies how many encodes can run at the same time 50% means 4 on a cpu with 8 threads one DEE can use 2 threads so 50% can utilize all threads (this option overrides the config's number) -p, --pipe MODE options: auto / always / never default: run -c/--config ffmpeg's audio goes into DEE without a temp .wav only works for DD/DDP/AC4/AAC and -mo, config: pipe -k, --keeptemp keep temp files -kl, --keep-log keep TrueHD's log and write a .deew-log.html report for each output -mo, --measure-only only measures the loudness of the source with DEE, no encoding, -f and the encoding options are ignored, TrueHD Atmos sources and Atmos masters are measured as Atmos -lb, --list-bitrates list bitrates that DEE can do for each format -la, --long-argument print ffmpeg, truehdd and DEE arguments for each input -np, --no-prompt skip confirmation questions, print them as notes and continue -pl, --print-logos show all logo variants you can set in the config -cl, --changelog show changelog -c, --config show config and config location -gc, --generate-config generate a new config, asks before overwriting an existing config (-np skips the question) -gt, --get-tools download ffmpeg, ffprobe, truehdd and dee_shim next to deew blue: uses dee_shim ``` # GUI - download `deew-gui` / `deew-gui.exe` / `deew-gui-macos` from [https://github.com/pcrlnd/deew/releases](https://github.com/pcrlnd/deew/releases) and put it in the same folder as the CLI binary (it looks for `deew` next to itself, `deew.exe` on Windows) - on Linux/macOS make the binaries executable: `chmod +x deew deew-gui` (`chmod +x deew-macos deew-gui-macos` on macOS) - Linux needs the WebKitGTK runtime: `libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0` (Debian/Ubuntu), `webkit2gtk4.1` (Fedora), `webkit2gtk-4.1` (Arch) - Windows 10/11 already include the needed `WebView2` runtime - the GUI has its own version number, independent from the CLI - build from source: `cd gui && npm install && npm run tauri build -- --no-bundle` (the binary will be in `gui/target/release/`), for development use `npm run tauri dev` - more details (development, web mode, security notes): [GUI readme](https://github.com/pcrlnd/deew/blob/main/gui/README.md) # Web UI - `deew-web` is the GUI in your browser, can be handy for a headless server (no WebKit needed) - download `deew-web` / `deew-web.exe` / `deew-web-macos` from [https://github.com/pcrlnd/deew/releases](https://github.com/pcrlnd/deew/releases) and put it next to the CLI binary, - on Linux/macOS run `chmod +x deew-web` (`chmod +x deew-web-macos` on macOS) - run it and open [http://127.0.0.1:8765](http://127.0.0.1:8765), use `--host 0.0.0.0` to make it reachable from other machines - login: run the `deew-web --hash-password` command and paste the hash into your `config.toml` file - build from source: `cd gui && npm install && npm run build && cargo build -p deew-web --release` (the binary will be in `gui/target/release/`) # Examples `deew -i *thd`\ TrueHD -> DDP encoding `deew -b 768 -i *flac`\ DDP encoding at 768kbps `deew -f ddp-atmos -i *thd`\ TrueHD Atmos -> DDP Atmos encoding from the Atmos master (uses truehdd and dee_shim) `deew -f thd-atmos -i *thd`\ TrueHD Atmos -> TrueHD Atmos re-encode (16 elements, uses truehdd and dee_shim) `deew -f ac4-atmos -b 448 -i *thd`\ TrueHD Atmos -> AC4 Atmos encoding at 448kbps `deew -f ac4-ims -i *thd`\ TrueHD Atmos -> AC4 immersive stereo (`--ac4-ims-mode music` for music) `deew -f ddp-atmos -i master.atmos`\ DDP Atmos from a DAMF Atmos master (ADM BWF `.wav` works the same way) `deew -f dd -i *dts -k`\ `deew -f ddp -i *dts`\ encode multiple formats/bitrates while creating the temp file only once # Discussion and Support [https://t.me/deew_supp](https://t.me/deew_supp) # Donate If you like deew, you can support the people behind it on Ko-fi or with Monero. pcroland: - [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/pcrlnd) - Monero: ``` 42pcroLMNqQbs87sSuNNTk8E8XHD88NhnSAx3exA3s1mHWAAyKH1oBw7dScYVRx3VJhUZT96QZNeo9Uw2qL72kwoHxVBXmL ``` rainbaby (developer of truehdd and dee_shim): - Monero: ``` 47BgNcwYCWhSHB3WMd7CPLX3Yb4Kz8TCsGJaUmX7KqG895UKvixks6yje3GSa489XR97FLQMcUaSacAHbMbF2xWz7dvyX9U ```
